title: Multi-file `graph`: auto ids collide across files and \newtheorem from another file is ignored
description:
Problem: read_project parses each file separately, and parse() resets its block counter and environment set on every call. So auto ids (`bid = labels[0] if labels else f"{env}:{n}"`) collide across files.
- On the PFR blueprint (`mathgraph graph mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex --no-align`), 155 of 188 proofs share an id with another proof. `proof:5` covers five proofs in five chapters.
- DOT/JSON consumers therefore merge them: reading the graph by id gives 1,486 theorem->lemma proof dependencies, against 483 true ones (1,003 spurious).
- Collisions on the other blueprints: FLT 182/499 nodes, equational_theories 113/364, con-nf 46/239, LeanAPAP 41/92.
- A \newtheorem defined in a preamble file is ignored in the other files. equational_theories loses its 6 `metatheorem` blocks even when macros/common.tex is passed; con-nf loses 1.
- Nodes have a line but no file. Duplicate real labels (FLT `hardly_ramified`) produce two nodes with no warning.

Fix: make read_project parse the joined sources once, so environments apply everywhere and the counter runs across files. Map lines back to (file, line), add `file` to Block and to graph nodes, and report duplicate ids in the summary instead of collapsing them silently. Verified: PFR stays at 406 nodes / 188 proofs / 746 edges / 30 dangling, with 0 duplicate ids.

Review status: verified independently (all six blueprints re-run; the fix was tested and keeps PFR's published counts).
acceptance_criteria:
- A two-file unittest shows proof ids are unique and a preamble \newtheorem is honoured.
- All six blueprints have 0 duplicate ids.

title: Measure verify's false-`nonexistent` rate from ground-truth names (the 'zero false-alarm' claim was never measurable)
description:
Problem: README calls `nonexistent` 'exact in both directions' and 'sound', and says the existence check costs 'zero false-alarm'. It isn't so:
- `mathgraph verify "addition of natural numbers is commutative" Nat.add_comm` returns nonexistent.
- 11 of 44 author-written blueprint \lean names that exist in Mathlib come back nonexistent (e.g. fermatLastTheoremThree, Pairwise.countable_of_isOpen_disjoint).
- 50,724 of 245,543 Mathlib theorems (20.7%, excluding auxiliaries and instances) are absent from idx_mathlib.

The claim was never measurable:
- verify-bench draws the correct population only from names already in the index (`gold = [g for g in b.declared_lean if g in known]` in cmd_verify_bench).
- NonexistentIsSound.test_to_additive_reconstructions_stay_reachable draws its names from the same index rows verify checks. That is a tautology: only `assertTrue(gen)` can fail.

Fix:
- In verify-bench, draw the correct population from ground-truth names and all blueprint \lean names, indexed or not. Report the false-nonexistent rate with a CP interval.
- Rewrite the reachability test to sample from mathlib_elab.jsonl, or from a fixed list (Finset.addEnergy, Set.ext_iff, Nat.add_comm, Continuous.add). It fails today, so mark it @unittest.expectedFailure citing mathgraph-dem.2 and mathgraph-dem.4. When those land, it becomes an unexpected success that fails the run until the marker is removed.

The root-cause fixes are mathgraph-dem.2 and mathgraph-dem.4; this bead makes the defect visible and keeps it measured.

Review status: two reviewers independently, plus a direct reproduction (Nat.add_comm -> nonexistent, 2026-10-16).
acceptance_criteria:
- verify-bench prints the false-nonexistent rate with n and an interval.
- The rewritten reachability test exists, marked expectedFailure citing mathgraph-dem.2/mathgraph-dem.4.
- README wording is left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Library benchmark: the '~15% max precision' headline has no producing code
description:
Problem: README's opening paragraph says 'Maximum achievable precision is ~15% on the library benchmark'. Its table gives 14.6% 'max precision at any threshold (>= 5 answers)', while admitting 'the precision row has not been re-measured since the fix'.
- evaluate.py's only sweep maximises answer rate at target precision 0.90. Nothing computes max precision at >= 5 answers.
- evaluate.run needs an idx_eval with holdout files, and no doc or script builds one.

Re-measured with current code (`mathgraph index mathgraph-data/artifacts/mathlib.jsonl <dir> --holdout 0.02 --pmi-holdout 0.02`, then evaluate.run(n=1500, **LEX) plus an exhaustive (tau, delta) sweep): r@1 9.69%, r@5 23.23%, MRR 0.1465. Max precision:

| floor | max precision |
|---|---|
| >= 5 answers | 20.0% (1/5) |
| >= 10 | 16.7% (2/12) |
| >= 20 | 14.3% (3/21) |
| >= 50 | 13.9% (26/187) |

The holdout also leaks. expand_to_additive runs before the holdout draw, and twins copy their source's docstring; 12.1% of docstring'd idx_mathlib rows share their exact docstring with another row. So 'nothing is scored against text it trained on' is false for ~12% of probes. This is the same defect class as mathgraph-aec, which fixed the PFR half of the same sentence.

Fix:
- Add a max-precision-at->=k sweep over run's records to evaluate.py. bench_pfr.combined_precision_sweep already has the logic; add min_answers.
- Document the idx_eval build command.
- Dedupe docstrings, or draw holdouts before twin expansion, so twins never straddle the split.
- Choose a floor larger than one answer's worth of noise, and publish counts with the percentage.

Review status: two reviewers independently (one re-measured it).
acceptance_criteria:
- One documented command regenerates the library table, precision row included.
- A test shows holdout probes share no docstring with training rows.
- README's opening sentence is updated via mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Score the actual task: add a paper->mathlib arm to `mathgraph bench`
description:
Problem: every recall figure, threshold fit and verifier rate is measured on targets written alongside the paper (the paper's own formalization).
- harvest.py keeps only targets in the project's own Lean (`known = {d["name"] for d in decls}`; `targets = [t for t in b.declared_lean if t in known]`).
- bench_pfr's present arm is PFR's own declarations.

Across the six local blueprints there are 779 annotated statements. 634 target the project's own declarations and 36 a mathlib declaration (34 mathlib-only, 27 of them in idx_mathlib). Results on those 27 ('arm M'):

| ranker | r@1 / r@5 / r@10 |
|---|---|
| lexical and +structural | 3 / 3 / 4 |
| bge-small | 2 / 4 / 5 |
| bge-base | 2 / 3 / 3 |

At GRAPH_THRESHOLDS: 23 unmatched, 4 ambiguous, 0 matched. Lexical r@5 = 3/27 = 11% (Wilson 95% [3.9, 28.1]); the interval excludes the published 31.8%. No arm-M gold docstring copies its statement (median Jaccard 0.06), so this arm is also free of the mathgraph-dem.1 contamination.

Fix: add arm_mathlib() to bench_pfr / cmd_bench.
- Take the non-proof blocks (>= 5 words, per mathgraph-dr1.4) from all local blueprints whose \lean targets are in idx_mathlib and not in any project's own declarations.
- Score them on idx_mathlib.
- Report r@1/5/10 with Wilson CIs, plus status counts at GRAPH_THRESHOLDS.

Do NOT change harvest's fit output: evaluate.py and adapt.py fit and train on blueprint_pairs.jsonl, so adding mathlib targets there would leak the new arm into the fit set.

Review status: verified independently (arm re-derived: n=27, 3/27, 0 matched).
acceptance_criteria:
- `mathgraph bench` prints arm M with n, r@k with intervals, and status counts.
- A corpus test pins n = 27 on the pinned checkouts.
- mathgraph-luh.1 grows this arm; its README placement is left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Report held-out false matches (leave-one-project-out) and count wrong MATCHED answers
description:
Problem 1: 'zero false matches' is zero in-sample by construction. evaluate.sweep_zero_false sets delta to the largest fit-negative margin and skips any pair that admits a negative (the binding negative is LeanAPAP bohr-reg-def, margin 0.2656). Leave-one-project-out with the repo's own sweep:

| held-out project | false matches |
|---|---|
| FLT | 0/122 |
| LeanAPAP | 1/23 |
| carleson | 0/164 |
| con-nf | 0/53 |
| equational_theories | 9/76 |
| pooled | 10/438 = 2.3% (Clopper-Pearson 95% [1.1, 4.2]) |

54 of the 438 negatives share an identical (coverage, margin) with another. Errors cluster by project, so the valid calibration unit is the project, and with 6 projects any per-new-project bound is weak. mathgraph-luh.1 grows the pool.

Problem 2: 'zero false' counts only absent-arm matches (the code says 'Answered-not-rank-1 is not a false match here'). At the shipped pair, the fit's present arm answers 16, and 5 of those are wrong:
- wiggle-order-1 and wiggle-order-2 -> wiggle_order_100
- 387_implies_43, 14_implies_29 and 3744_implies_3722_381 -> `implying`

That is a matched precision of 11/16 = 68.8% [41.3, 89.0] (9/14 on the unvalidated corpus). README prints the answered and correct counts but never names the 5 errors.

Fix:
- Carry the project label through graph_arms.
- Add a ~10-line LOPO loop to `evaluate.py graph` that refits on the other projects and counts held-out false matches. Print the pooled held-out count with a CP interval.
- Add `wrong = answered - correct` to sweep_zero_false's output.
- Wherever the operating point is described, report answered / correct / wrong / absent-arm false.

Review status: verified independently (LOPO re-run with the repo's own sweep; the 5 wrong answers re-checked).
acceptance_criteria:
- `python -m mathgraph.evaluate graph ...` prints in-sample answered/correct/wrong and the LOPO held-out false matches with an interval.
- A unittest on a synthetic 3-project record set checks the LOPO arithmetic.
- README wording is left to mathgraph-dem.12.

Review status: plan bead; the stale figures listed below were each confirmed by at least one reviewer.

title: Report present-arm MATCHED at the shipped thresholds; '100% correct abstention' is indistinguishable from always-abstain
description:
Problem: at GRAPH_THRESHOLDS (0.2526/0.2658) the tool matches nothing on PFR.
- Present arm: 0 of 176 answerable statements matched (170 unmatched, 6 ambiguous). 3 of the 6 ambiguous have gold at rank 1, but their margins are 0.065-0.168.
- Absent arm: 0 of 174 matched (169 unmatched, 5 ambiguous). The largest margin over all 174 is 0.2473, below every delta_margin ever shipped (0.2649-0.2722). So this arm cannot produce a false match at any shipped threshold, and an always-abstain baseline scores identically.

So README's 'abstention is perfect on real paper text' and cli.py's 'nor on the PFR absent arm' say nothing about calibration. Related problems:
- tests/test_corpus.py's test_thresholds_are_actually_engaged says it guards against 'nothing is ever answered', but it only asserts tau_cov > 0 and delta_margin > 0.
- README's '5.7%' PFR answer rate counts AMBIGUOUS as answered (bench_pfr counts `status != UNMATCHED`).

Fix:
- Count MATCHED (and correct MATCHED) in arm_present at the shipped thresholds, and print it beside the absent-arm table.
- Add an always-abstain baseline row.
- Make the engagement test assert >= 1 MATCHED on the 439-pair fit arm (16 today).
- Count MATCHED, not `status != UNMATCHED`, wherever an answer rate is reported.

This makes the negative conclusion stronger; restate it, never soften it. README wording is left to mathgraph-dem.12; a suggestion: '0 false and 0 true matches on PFR at the shipped thresholds; indistinguishable from always-abstain'.

Review status: verified independently (own script: 0/176 matched, max absent margin 0.2473).
acceptance_criteria:
- Bench output includes present-arm matched/correct at the shipped thresholds, plus the always-abstain baseline.
- The engagement test fails if the thresholds answer nothing on the fit arm.

title: Pin corpus revisions and record them in every index and release
description:
Problem: setup clones mathlib4 (`git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse`) and every blueprint (`git clone --depth 1`) at HEAD, with no revision. meta.json records counts but no commit, and README/QUICKSTART name none. So a fresh `mathgraph setup` builds a different corpus, and none of these can be reproduced anywhere else:
- the arm sizes (176/174)
- the 251,236-declaration index
- every recall figure
- the GRAPH_THRESHOLDS fit

Absent-arm labels also decay silently as mathlib absorbs PFR results; 5 PFR statements already resolve by exact name. Re-harvesting the current checkouts with current code gives 441 pairs, not the pinned 439 (3 new, 1 missing).

The published numbers come from these checkouts:
| repo | commit |
|---|---|
| mathlib4 | b44f89d15d463ede557bdf673707a8610210becf |
| pfr | 68730da4cb35f07c6928e3b5b32e177b7ab97c36 |
| carleson | 020d6e5c71d731952eb0379d222eea4049103ca0 |
| FLT | 4025558e4756e7ab9e1552f957706a7caf86cb42 |
| equational_theories | 7e276a2d05e84e3eef02432abfd0718e78f7abfa |
| con-nf | 55b939a3acf947793e252ff330800bfe968cc172 |
| LeanAPAP | afafc42a5326d770d0f853f060b2f63947c13f0f |

Fix:

title: One operating point: Aligner's constructor defaults are a superseded threshold pair and stale weights
description:
Problem: Aligner.__init__ defaults to `tau_cov=0.2474, delta_margin=0.2671, mod_weight=0.35, prefix_weight=0.7, title_boost=1.6`. The shipped values are:
- cli.LEX: mod_weight=0.1, prefix_weight=0.85, title_boost=2.5, len_pivot=0.75, typ_weight=0.15
- cli.GRAPH_THRESHOLDS: tau_cov=0.2526, delta_margin=0.2658

0.2474/0.2671 is the pair that cli.py's own history comment records as admitting false matches; measured now, it admits 3 of 438 on the blueprint negative arm. bench_pfr.main builds `Aligner(load(...), **kw)` from argv only. Consequences:
- README's absent-arm reproduce command passes LEX but no thresholds, so it measures 168/6/0 (the published figure) at the old pair. At the shipped pair it is 169/5/0.
- README's 'What does work' block (183 unmatched / 12 ambiguous) reproduces at neither pair. `mathgraph graph` prints 186/9 at the shipped pair and 185/10 at the constructor defaults.
- Constructor weights + GRAPH_THRESHOLDS without LEX gives 170/4/0. That is the mechanism behind the 170/4 figure that mathgraph-p14 closed as 'transcription error, no mechanism found': sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-1f3.md built its Aligner with **GRAPH_THRESHOLDS and no **LEX.
- bench_pfr.main's default pattern is /home/claude/pfr/..., which matches 0 blocks and raises ZeroDivisionError after a 1.1 GB index load.
- bench_dense keeps its own copy of LEX, without typ_weight.

Fix: define LEX and GRAPH_THRESHOLDS once in align.py as Aligner's defaults, and import them in cli.py. Default bench_pfr's pattern from MATHGRAPH_DATA (as freeze_bench already does) and its thresholds from GRAPH_THRESHOLDS; JSON on argv can still override. Make bench_dense import LEX.

Review status: found independently by four reviewers with consistent numbers; the constructor defaults were also checked directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- `Aligner(art)` with no kwargs equals the shipped configuration (unittest).
- `uv run python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr` with no argument runs on the shipped config.
- README's corrected breakdowns and the p14 mechanism note land via mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Strip PFR docstrings from idx_full's PMI table and bench_pretrained's corpus text (test-set leakage)
description:
Problem: the present-arm numbers are measured with the test answers' own text inside the model.
- 77 of 168 PFR present-arm statements have a gold declaration whose docstring copies the blueprint statement nearly verbatim (word-Jaccard >= 0.5). Example: blueprint 'Projection entropy and distance' (distance.tex) vs the docstring of ent_of_proj_le in pfr.jsonl.
- index.build trains the English->token PMI table on every row with a docstring (the loop skips only `not r.get("doc") or id(r) in pmi_blocked`, and pmi_blocked is empty without --pmi-holdout). idx_full = mathlib + pfr.jsonl (setup_cmd's combine step), so 461 of 1,065 PFR rows' docstrings train it. Example: `conjecture` -> `pfr` exists only through PFR docs; 116 words change their token set when PFR docs are withheld.
- bench_pretrained embeds name + doc + head for every corpus row, PFR's included.

Measured with PFR docstrings withheld: present-arm lexical r@1/r@5 = 15.9%/27.8% (published 18.2%/31.8%; the Aligner.align path gives 18.8%/31.8%). +structural r@5 goes 38.1% -> 33.0%, and the combined sweep's 100%-precision point moves from 3/350 to 5/350. For bge-small (br3), r@1 goes 26.1% -> 5.1% and precision at 10% coverage 20/35 -> 1/34. br3's error analysis ('the ceiling is ranking among near-duplicates') rests on the copied text.

This contradicts cli.py's comment that LEX was fit 'with PFR held out', and README's statement that PFR docstrings are the test set (adapt.py excludes them for the dense encoder; the lexical path never did).

Fix: drop `doc` from PFR rows where setup combines pfr.jsonl into idx_full (or add a module-prefix exclusion such as pmi_skip_prefix="PFR." to index.build's PMI loop). Record the exclusion in meta.json and bump INDEX_VERSION. Make bench_pretrained's doc_text drop docstrings for non-mathlib rows.

Review status: verified independently (lexical figures reproduced; +structural/sweep figures from the reporter's run).
acceptance_criteria:
- idx_full's PMI table gets no contribution from PFR docstrings: a unittest on a tiny fixture shows a word that appears only in a PFR-prefixed row's doc is absent from `trans`.
- meta.json records the exclusion; INDEX_VERSION is bumped.
- Handoff reports paired lost/gained on the present arm against the current index. README numbers are left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: leanscan regex defects drop ~9.3k real Mathlib names and index ~7.1k names that don't exist
description:
Problem: `uv run mathgraph verify "addition of natural numbers is commutative" Nat.add_comm` returns `nonexistent`. This bead covers one root cause, leanscan's regexes; the other is mathgraph-dem.4. Probe results with the real scan_file:
- Inside `namespace Foo`, `theorem _root_.Bar.baz` is indexed as `Foo._root_.Bar.baz` (3,634 scraped names contain `_root_`).
- `public theorem`, `meta` declarations, `instance (priority := 100) foo`, `alias ⟨a, b⟩` and `open Nat in theorem ...` produce nothing.
- `noncomputable section X ... end X`, `public section`, `mutual` blocks and `end X -- comment` lose the namespace.
- Non-Greek Unicode identifiers are truncated (`def compₘ` becomes `Foo.comp`), and `univ.{u}` becomes `Foo.univ.`.
- Block comments `/- -/` are scanned as code.

Measured against the elaborated ground truth (mathlib_elab.jsonl): fixing all of these raises idx_mathlib's names-found-in-the-environment from 240,034 to 249,310. It also cuts non-private indexed names that are absent from the environment from 7,146 to 1,914. About 520 truncated identifiers carry another real declaration's name. For about 142 of them the phantom row wins verify's name2id lookup (last row wins), so verify checks the wrong declaration (e.g. OrderHom.comp <- compₘ).

Fix (all in leanscan.py):
- Strip a leading `_root_.` instead of prefixing the namespace.
- Add `public` and `meta` to the modifiers.
- Skip `(priority := ...)` and a leading `open ... in`.
- Emit both names of `alias ⟨a, b⟩`.
- Let the section regex accept `(noncomputable|public) section` and `mutual`, and the end regex a trailing `--` comment.
- Widen the identifier class to any non-delimiter character, and drop `.{u}`.
- Skip `/- -/` blocks.

Review status: verified independently (probe results and before/after counts reproduced).
acceptance_criteria:
- A probe .lean fixture covering every case above is checked in as a unittest and passes.
- A rescan of mathlib reports found-in-environment and phantom counts before/after (expect roughly +9.3k and -5.2k).
- Handoff reports the paired effect on the present and absent arms. README numbers are left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Score pretrained mathlib retrievers against the gold negative arm (precision at coverage)
description: Discovery shortlist #1 (portfolio notes/discovery-shortlist.md). No published mathlib retriever has been evaluated on statements with no counterpart: LeanSearch v2 (arXiv 2605.13137) drops such queries, Lean Finder (2510.15940) reports Recall/MRR only, and TheoremGraph (2606.25363) reports LLM-judged precision by tier with no gold negatives. mathgraph's frozen benchmark has a gold negative arm (PFR blueprint: 174 absent / 176 present) and a scorer where null = abstain, but only in-house retrievers have been scored on it. Score LeanSearch v2, Lean Finder and a TheoremGraph-style slogan embedding with a similarity/margin abstention threshold via bench_dense.py. FIRST re-audit the absent arm's gold labels for statements mathlib covers in paraphrase: TheoremGraph found 65% of its high-cosine misses were valid restatements.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-registered before scoring: the threshold rule and the coverage points (1%, 5%, 10%, 20%). Report precision/recall/absent-arm false-match rate per system with Wilson CIs; the gold-label audit is documented with the number of relabels; the verdict on >=90% precision at >=10% coverage is stated with its CI, whichever way it goes.
notes:
PRE-REGISTRATION, 2026-09-24, before any scoring.
Systems: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 (pretrained general-purpose dense encoders, sentence-transformers, CPU), plus the existing lexical aligner as the baseline. Lean Finder (delta-lab-ai/lean-finder, 8.2B Qwen3) is out of reach on 16 GB, and LeanSearch-PS is a proof-state adapter; both are recorded as NOT tested.
Doc text: '<name>. <doc>. <head>'. Query text: '<title>. <text>' from bench_pfr.blueprint_blocks (the same blocks every earlier mathgraph number used). The present arm is scored against idx_full, the absent arm against idx_mathlib (idx_full minus PFR rows), with the corpus embedded once.
Answer rule: answer iff top-1 cosine >= t. A margin variant (top1 - top2 >= t) is reported alongside. A present-arm answer is correct iff top-1 is in gold; an absent-arm answer is wrong UNLESS the label audit finds a genuine mathlib counterpart.
Report precision at coverage 1/5/10/20% of the pooled arms, with Wilson 95% CIs. Verdict: >=90% precision at >=10% coverage, stated with its Wilson lower bound.
Label audit: every absent-arm statement answered at the 10%-coverage threshold by either model is hand-checked for a genuine mathlib counterpart, and relabels are counted and listed.
RESULT 2026-09-24 (README 'Pretrained encoders, as precision at coverage'). Pooled n=350 (176 present / 174 absent). bge-small-en-v1.5: recall@1 26.1%, precision@10% 20/35 = 57.1% [Wilson 40.9, 72.0]. bge-base-en-v1.5: recall@1 31.3%, precision@10% 20/35 = 57.1% [40.9, 72.0], after 1 relabel. 90%@10% is EXCLUDED at 95% confidence for both. Margin rule: 51-57%. Errors at 10%: absent-arm false 2/4, present-arm wrong top-1 13/11 (sibling PFR decls). Audit: 5 distinct absent statements checked against mathlib source, 1 relabel (indepFun_prod = two-variable case of the gold independent_copies_two).
close_reason: Pre-registered protocol run for two pretrained encoders; verdict: neither reaches 90% precision at 10% coverage (Wilson upper bound 72%). Audit done (1 relabel of 5). Lean Finder / LeanSearch v2 not runnable on 16 GB, split out as a follow-up.

title: mathgraph/freeze_bench.py main() crashes: hardcoded artifact names idx_deploy/idx_mathlib_only don't exist
description:

    deploy = {r["name"] for r in load("idx_deploy")["rows"]}
    mathlib = {r["name"] for r in load("idx_mathlib_only")["rows"]}

title: `mathgraph query` never abstains: a nonsense query scores 1.0
description:
Problem: cmd_query builds the Aligner with tau_cov=0 and delta_margin=0, and prints only ranked candidates, with no status. In the default struct mode, StructReranker normalises by the top score (`smax = float(scores[0]) or 1.0`; `float(sc) / smax + lam * st`), so the top hit scores >= 1.0 by construction.
- `mathgraph query "purple elephants dance quietly under bridges" --topk 2` returns SimpleGraph.IsBridge with score 1.0.
- With --rerank none, the same query prints raw coverage (19.5976) under the same `score` key.

So the documented first command shows a 'perfect' score for an unrelated lemma -- the nearest-plausible-lemma failure the README says the tool exists to prevent.

Fix:
- In cmd_query, also run al.align at GRAPH_THRESHOLDS, and print its status (matched/ambiguous/unmatched) with raw coverage and margin next to the ranked list.
- Rename the struct-path field to rel_score, or document that it is relative to the top hit.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified (follows directly from the code).
acceptance_criteria:
- The nonsense query prints `unmatched`.
- Scores are labelled consistently across rerank modes.

- CLAUDE.md's Build & Test / Architecture / Conventions sections are the unfilled template, and AGENTS.md has no project content.
- The working test command (`uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests`, ~4 min; corpus tests skip without mathgraph-data) appears in five inconsistent versions. QUICKSTART uses bare `python`, which isn't on PATH here.
- The repo's central rule ('A number in a document is only allowed to exist if the code produces it or the document says where it came from') lives only in sandbox-prompt.md, which interactive sessions never load.

Fix:
- sandbox-prompt.md: replace 'Known baseline' and 'First objective' with the current state and point at the open beads. Quote README's current headline, and drop the chown sentence.
- SKILL.md: stop pasting outputs ('compare against README Benchmarks'). Fix the error type and test count, and delete the stale-corpus gotcha and the 'main twice' note.
- CLAUDE.md: fill it in ~10 lines -- the uv test command and its runtime, the skip behaviour and the skip-intolerant form from mathgraph-ltq.2, the provenance rule, and a pointer to the run-mathgraph skill.
- AGENTS.md: add 'Project rules: see CLAUDE.md'.
- QUICKSTART: fix the test command.

Review status: single reviewer; the sandbox-prompt.md staleness was confirmed by reading the file directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- No stale figure remains in these files.
- CLAUDE.md has the commands and the provenance rule.

title: Remove cade.py: unrelated code that fabricates candidates and reports success it did not achieve
description:
Problem: mathgraph/cade.py, tests/test_cade.py and the `mathgraph cade` subcommands in cli.py came in for mathgraph-fbk, which was filed for a separate chem project's robot-actuation loop. README and QUICKSTART never mention it.
- `if not candidates and "H4 chain" in content:` fabricates four H4 molecules in production code.
- Candidate ids use `hash(structure)`, which is salted per process: two runs gave cand_water_d6577f89, then cand_water_353282f8.
- `mathgraph cade feedback /nonexistent/cand.json --verdict-ok --actuation-success` substitutes a 'Mock Candidate', prints `"certificate_status": "VERIFIED"`, `"loop_closed": true` and `"action_taken": "Logged and archived in CADE history"`, and exits 0. Nothing is archived.
- json, parse, Block and Generator are imported but unused.

It is the only code in a tool whose claim is abstention that invents output, and its 5 tests gate every bead.

Fix: delete the module, its tests and its CLI wiring. Don't patch the hash or the mock path. If the chem project needs it, it belongs there, importing mathgraph.latex if it wants the parser.

Review status: single reviewer; the mock-candidate 'VERIFIED' output was reproduced directly on 2026-10-16.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -rn cade mathgraph tests` finds nothing.
- The suite is green.

title: Decide the license; make pyproject, LICENSE.md and the data card agree; add notices for third-party data
description:
DECISION NEEDED FROM THE OWNER: which license covers the code -- the Big Time Public License 2.0.0 (LICENSE.md) or Apache-2.0 (pyproject)? This bead is deferred so the sandbox loop never dispatches it.

Problems:
- LICENSE.md is the Big Time Public License 2.0.0, but pyproject.toml says `license = { text = "Apache-2.0" }`, so any tool reading the SPDX metadata treats the package as Apache-2.0.
- README's shipped-benchmark section and freeze_bench's data card say the release 'inherits Apache 2.0', but the release also contains this repo's scorer code.
- .dockerignore excludes LICENSE.md, so the image carries the Apache metadata without the license file.
- Committed derived data (blueprint_pairs.jsonl, tasks.jsonl, mathgraph-data/artifacts/blueprint_pairs.jsonl) is statement text from Apache-2.0 repos (con-nf: Apache/MIT). Apache section 4 requires a copy of the license and attribution, and the repo has no NOTICE or attribution file.
- 632 rows come from lean4-ergodic-theory, whose URL, commit and license are recorded nowhere.
- Also: pyproject's Homepage is https://github.com/YOURNAME/mathgraph (the remote is B0001/mathgraph); the `train = []` extra installs nothing; lean/DumpDecls.lean, which leanast loads via dirname(dirname(__file__)), is not in the wheel.

Fix, after the decision:
- Set `license = { file = "LICENSE.md" }` (or the chosen SPDX id).
- Stop excluding LICENSE.md from the Docker context, and copy it into the image.
- State in the data card that the statements inherit Apache-2.0 from their sources, while scorer.py is under the repo license.
- Add a DATA-LICENSES/NOTICE section listing each source repo's URL, pinned commit and license.
- Record the ergodic rows' source, or drop them.
- Fix Homepage and delete the empty extra.
- Either force-include DumpDecls.lean in the wheel, or document that elaborate needs a checkout.

Review status: two reviewers independently; LICENSE.md and pyproject were read directly.
acceptance_criteria:
- All license statements agree.
- Notices are present for third-party data.
notes: Owner decision needed (which license covers the code); a sandbox worker must not choose. Undefer once decided.

title: Benchmark tests call the real command code, not hand-copied replicas
description:
Problem: the tests copy the commands instead of calling them.
- Benchmark.setUpClass repeats cmd_bench step for step: the glob, the parse, the 5-word filter, `Aligner(..., tau_cov=0, delta_margin=0, **LEX)`, `StructReranker(lam=0.9, depth=10000)` and the h1/h5 loop.
- VerifyBenchAcceptRates repeats cmd_verify_bench.
- In the full suite, cli.py executes 0 of 238 lines, and bench_pfr.blueprint_blocks and bench_pfr.main are never called.

README cites the commands themselves (`uv run mathgraph bench`, `python -m mathgraph.bench_pfr ...`, `verify-bench --patterns`). So changing cmd_bench, cmd_verify_bench or bench_pfr.main moves published numbers while every test stays green. That is why no test caught mathgraph-dem.5's defaults or bench_pfr's crashing default path.

Fix:
- Move each command's body after load() into a function that takes (aligner, blocks) and returns the dict it prints.
- Have the commands print that dict, and have the tests call the same function with the cached aligner.
- Use bench_pfr.blueprint_blocks everywhere (mathgraph-dr1.4).

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- No duplicated benchmark loop remains in the tests.
- The tests exercise the same functions the CLI calls.

title: Corpus test runs must fail on unexpected skips
description:
Problem: `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/nonexistent uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests` prints `Ran 93 tests ... OK (skipped=24)` and exits 0.
- There are 14 skip sites, plus a silent fallback in a CoverageIsAFraction helper: `return qs or [("a compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed", "")]`. With no blueprint_pairs.jsonl it runs 1 query instead of 150, and passes.
- On a corpus built by `mathgraph setup` without Lean, CoverageIsAFraction skips entirely because its class decorator needs idx_elaborated. That includes test_never_negative, which only uses idx_full.
- In parallel mode (max-parallel > 1), verified-sandbox mounts a git worktree as each worker's /workspace. mathgraph-data is gitignored, so unless it is mounted separately, those workers' corpus tests always skip and still print OK.

Fix:
- When MATHGRAPH_DATA is set explicitly, make skips fail (raise AssertionError instead of SkipTest).
- Delete the silent fallback.
- Let CoverageIsAFraction's idx_full checks run without idx_elaborated.
- Document the skip-intolerant one-liner for corpus runs: `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests 2>&1 | grep -qx OK`.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified (the parallel-sandbox point was read from verified-sandbox's loop.sh).
acceptance_criteria:
- A corpus run with a missing artifact fails.
- The no-corpus run stays green for the unit tests.
- CLAUDE.md and sandbox-prompt.md use the skip-intolerant form (coordinate with mathgraph-431.6).

title: No-corpus smoke test through cli.main (scan -> index -> query -> verify -> graph)
description:
Problem: a 0.1-second fixture -- a ~10-line Lean file and two 2-line .tex files in a tempdir, driven through cli.main -- covers 818 of 1,275 lines in the 9 core modules (64%). The full 195-second suite covers 720 of them, and only 271 without the corpus.

Run today, the fixture shows:
- the scanner bugs (mathgraph-dem.2): `public theorem pub_thm` is not scanned, so verify says nonexistent; `_root_.Bar.rooted` is scanned as `Foo._root_.Bar.rooted`
- the graph-id collision (mathgraph-cxh.1): ids come out ['thm:a','proof:2','thm:b','proof:2']

It catches verify-bench's filtering or the cross-file \newtheorem case only if the fixture includes them.

Fix: one test class in tests/test_units.py.
- Write the fixture, including a \newtheorem in a.tex that b.tex uses.
- Call cli.main for scan, index, query, verify and graph.
- Assert the scanned names, unique graph ids, the query's top-1 and the verify status.
- Put the cases that fail today in their own methods, marked @unittest.expectedFailure citing mathgraph-dem.2 or mathgraph-cxh.1. They turn into unexpected successes, which fail the run, once those fixes land.

Review status: partially verified: the coverage gap and the failures were reproduced, but the fixture alone catches only part of the scanner and graph bugs.
acceptance_criteria: - The test runs in < 1 s with no corpus and fails if any of those commands breaks.

title: Register every \label and resolve refs through it; match nested \end; drop self-loops
description:
Problem: only a block's first \label becomes its id, and refs resolve against block ids alone.
- On PFR: 13 proofs are named after an inner equation (e.g. `lhs-to-bound`). That produces 11 self-loop depends_on edges, all counted inside the published 746.
- 29 of PFR's 30 published 'dangling refs' are labels that sit inside a parsed block (16 real cross-block edges, 13 self).
- The more-random dependency through `pqr-defs` (torsion.tex) is lost at proof level.
- Carleson: 73 label-named proofs, 55 self-loops, 301 of 604 dangling refs resolvable (190 cross-block, 111 self), and a 3-cycle in what README calls a DAG.
- A nested proof ends at the inner \end{proof}, so refs after it vanish, and the outer proof takes the inner claim's label.

Fix:
- Match \end by nesting depth of the same environment.
- Take the id from the first \label outside nested math/theorem environments, otherwise the auto id.
- Map every label to its block and resolve refs through that map.
- Drop src == dst edges.
- Then re-run PFR, and replace README's '746 internal edges · 30 dangling' block and the 'The internal graph is exact' sentence. Say what 'exact' means: no invented edges. This bead owns that README block.

Review status: verified independently (PFR figures reproduced; Carleson cycle confirmed).
acceptance_criteria:
- A unittest covers the nested-proof and inner-equation cases.
- README's graph figures are regenerated by `mathgraph graph`.

title: proves edges are guessed from adjacency; \proves{} and [Proof of \ref{..}] are ignored
description:
Problem: latex.parse sets `blk.proof_of = last_theorem` for every proof, and cuts the `[...]` title off before extracting refs.
- Carleson chapter/main.tex has `\begin{proof}[Proof of \Cref{metric-space-Carleson}] \leanok \proves{metric-space-Carleson}`. It gets a proves edge to `int-continuous`, and none to metric-space-Carleson.
- 35 of 39 Carleson \proves proofs, and 8 of 8 FLT ones, point at the wrong statement.
- 40 \Cref commands in Carleson proof titles are dropped.

Deferred proofs are standard in arXiv papers. No published number reads proves edges; PFR's proofs follow their statements.

Fix:
- Set proof_of from the body's \proves{X}; otherwise from a single ref in the raw title; otherwise fall back to adjacency.
- Run the ref regex over the raw title too.
- Add `"source": "proves"|"title"|"adjacent"` to the edge in graph.py.

Review status: verified independently (35/39 Carleson and 8/8 FLT mismatches re-counted).
acceptance_criteria:
- A deferred-proof unittest sits next to the existing adjacent-proof test.
- Carleson and FLT \proves proofs have 0 mismatches.

title: Add the lean4-ergodic-theory negatives as a second absent arm; call PFR a development set
description:
Problem: PFR has steered design choices, yet README still calls it 'the test set'. Examples:
- typ_weight is justified by 'PFR r@1 collapses from 18.9% to 13.1%'.
- Per-field max_df gating was rejected on a PFR table.
- A refit was triggered by PFR false matches.
- 'Hand weights helped on PFR'.

Meanwhile the root blueprint_pairs.jsonl holds 632 lean4-ergodic-theory pairs that never entered threshold fitting or lexical evaluation. They were adapt.py training data and fed structmatch's gate design, so they are not untouched. Scored once against idx_mathlib at the shipped thresholds: 624 unmatched, 8 ambiguous, 0 matched, max margin 0.2545 (CP95 upper bound 0.58%). Unlike PFR, this arm can fail: the LeanAPAP-held-out LOPO thresholds produce 1 false match on it.

Caveats:
- Median statement length is 42 words, vs 13 for PFR.
- Labels are exact-name lookups.
- The source repo's URL, commit and license are recorded nowhere (mathgraph-431.2).

Fix:
- Add the ergodic arm as a second absent arm in the abstention evaluation: filter project == lean4-ergodic-theory from the root pairs and score on idx_mathlib at GRAPH_THRESHOLDS. Report 0/632 with its CP bound.
- Disclose its prior use and the length gap.
- Call PFR the development set. A sealed, untouched test set comes from mathgraph-luh.1.

Review status: partially verified (the ergodic arm was re-scored; the 'never used' wording was corrected: the pairs fed adapt.py and structmatch's gate design).
acceptance_criteria:
- The ergodic arm is computed by code and pinned in a corpus test.
- README wording is left to mathgraph-dem.12.
- Keep root blueprint_pairs.jsonl, or move the ergodic rows under mathgraph-data/artifacts; mathgraph-431.4 must not delete them.

title: Verifier profiles: score `balanced` on PFR and make profile refits held-out
description:
Problems:
- cmd_verify_bench and its test only run `permissive` and `precise`. So `balanced` -- the one profile moved by in-sample selection on all 439 pairs (23.5% -> 26.2%) -- has never been scored on held-out PFR. Scored by the review (seed 0, no patterns):

| population | accepted |
|---|---|
| correct | 26/176 = 14.8% [9.9, 20.9] |
| sibling | 4/176 |
| wrong-namespace | 2/21 = 9.5% |
| hallucinated, random | 0 |

- The held-out check that showed in-fold dominance vanishing is one alphabetical split: fit on FLT, carleson and equational_theories; hold out LeanAPAP and con-nf (76 pairs). That is too small to resolve the 3-statement gains it judges (9.2% -> 13.2% is 7/76 vs 10/76), and it was never applied to the shipped constants.
- `python -m mathgraph.evaluate verify ./mathgraph-data/artifacts` no longer reproduces README's validated-corpus tables. It now gives precise 18.5/16.6/0.0, balanced 27.6/29.4/0.0 and permissive 40.8/65.1/0.0, against the published 18.7/17.5, 26.9/28.2 and 41.0/64.9/0.2. The precise refit now dominates held-out by +-1 of 76 (noise by README's one-statement rule), so 'Not one of them still dominates' is false as written. The '227 / 52 / 70 alternatives' figures are printed by no command.

Fix:
- Add `balanced` to cmd_verify_bench and its test.
- Replace the single split with five-fold leave-one-project-out, require dominance in every fold before moving a profile, and run the same check on the shipped profiles.
- Have `evaluate verify` print the in-sample alternative counts, or drop that sentence.

Review status: two reviewers independently; not adversarially verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- verify-bench reports all three profiles.
- `evaluate verify` prints LOPO results.
- README updates are left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Bench metrics: tie-safe recall@k, k/n with intervals, paired McNemar
description:
Problems:
- Ties. split_name drops primes, so `foo` and `foo'` always score identically, and Aligner's argpartition/argsort orders exact ties arbitrarily. 23 of 176 present-arm statements have a non-gold candidate tied with gold. r@1 is 31/176 = 17.6% if ties go against gold and 33/176 = 18.8% if they go for it. The published 18.2% (cmd_bench, depth 10000) and 18.8% (arm_present, depth 10) are just two tie orders. That is the root cause behind mathgraph-7dw, which was closed by documenting both numbers.
- Intervals. None of the headline rates carries one, e.g.:

| rate | 95% interval |
|---|---|
| abstention 174/174 | [97.9, 100] |
| precision 3/3 | [29.2, 100] |
| r@1 32/176 | [12.8, 24.7] |
| precise wrong-namespace 0/21 | [0, 16.1] |

  Only br3 reports intervals (bench_pretrained.wilson).
- Paired tests. The structural reranker's gain is r@1 32 vs 34 (discordant 7 vs 9, exact McNemar p = 0.80) and r@5 56 vs 67 (8 vs 19, p = 0.052). Yet README calls it 'the first thing in this repository that beats the lexical baseline' and quotes relative lifts that match no table. README's own rule says one-statement deltas are inside the noise floor.

Fix:
- Count a hit at rank k only if fewer than k non-gold candidates score >= the best gold score (request topk+1 to see the boundary).
- Print k/n and a Wilson (or exact) interval beside every rate in bench_pfr, cmd_bench and cmd_verify_bench, reusing bench_pretrained.wilson.
- Print discordant counts and an exact McNemar p for each reranker-vs-lexical comparison (~6 stdlib lines).

Review status: tie analysis and McNemar from single reviewers (consistent with each other); intervals computed by the review.
acceptance_criteria:
- Both PFR code paths report the same tie-safe r@1.
- Unittests cover the tie rule and the McNemar arithmetic.
- README restatements are left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: One shared PFR arm definition: labels from code, not prose; disclose the 5-word filter
description:
Problems:
- Labels come from exact-name lookup: a statement is a negative iff none of its \lean names is in idx_mathlib. 3 of the 174 absent-arm statements have gold names that resolve in no index, and are filed as negatives anyway: energy-def (`Finset.addEnergy'`), cs-bound (`Finset.card_sq_le_card_mul_addEnergy'`) and bsg (`BSG`), all AddCombi names.
- cs-bound has a genuine counterpart in idx_mathlib: `Finset.card_sq_le_card_mul_addEnergy` (Mathlib/Combinatorics/Additive/Energy.lean; with s=t=A, u=B it is the blueprint inequality). So README's 'no correct answer anywhere in the index' is false for that row.
- br3's relabel (independent copies -> ProbabilityTheory.indepFun_prod) exists only in README prose. The stored br3_BAAI__bge-base-en-v1.5.json gives 19/35 at 10% coverage, README reports 20/35 (57%), and bench_pretrained still scores every absent-arm answer as wrong.
- Only br3's 5 answered negatives were ever audited (1 relabelled); none of the 174 PFR or 438 fit negatives were. A last-name check also flags ProbabilityTheory.IsUniform vs MeasureTheory.pdf.IsUniform, plus goursat, finrank and tau.
- An undisclosed filter `len(b.text.split()) >= 5` drops 33 of the 212 annotated PFR statements. All 33 are formula-only ('We have MATH', 'One has MATH') and have their gold in idx_full. README says '179 annotated statements' and never mentions the rule. The filter is copied 4 times: bench_pfr.blueprint_blocks, cli.cmd_bench, cli.cmd_verify_bench and the tests.

Fix:
- Add one module-level AUDITED relabel dict in bench_pfr (cs-bound, plus the br3 statement).
- Make blueprint_blocks drop and count statements whose names resolve in no index.
- Make cmd_bench, cmd_verify_bench, freeze_bench, bench_pretrained and the tests import blueprint_blocks and the labels instead of re-deriving them.
- Report the 5-word filter and the dropped count in bench output, and report present-arm recall over all 209 indexed-gold statements beside the 176 figure.

Auditing every threshold-clearing negative (31 by coverage and 19 by margin on the fit arm, 5 on PFR) can follow as its own bead.

Review status: label claims verified independently (cs-bound, unresolvable names, br3 19/35); the 5-word-filter claim is from a single reviewer.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every harness uses a single definition of the arms; grep finds no other copy of the filter.
- Bench output reports the dropped and relabelled counts.
- br3 precision recomputed from code matches what the README will state (mathgraph-dem.12).

title: index.load never checks index_version; idx_elaborated is a stale pre-fix artifact
description:
Problem: nothing checks whether an index is current.
- index.load only unpickles.
- cli._art only checks that the file exists.
- needs_build runs only in setup, which never builds idx_elaborated.

`mathgraph query --corpus idx_elaborated ...` therefore loads the 2026-07-28 artifact with no warning. Its meta has no index_version or ground_truth_decls. 24,804 of its rows (5.3%) carry type tokens cut at the first `:=`, which the current builder no longer produces. That fix landed on 2026-07-31 in 61ef518, the same commit that wrote README's idx_elaborated numbers.

Fix: in index.load, compare meta's index_version with INDEX_VERSION and fail (or warn loudly) with the rebuild command. Rebuild idx_elaborated with the toolchain-free half of cmd_elaborate (to_index_rows -> merge_docs -> build), using the existing mathlib_elab_raw.jsonl.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- Loading an index with a missing or old index_version raises an error with a rebuild hint (unittest).
- idx_elaborated is rebuilt with current meta.
- README's idx_elaborated figures are re-measured in mathgraph-dem.12.

title: argmatch splits Lean arguments at ';' instead of truncating there
description:
Problem: argmatch's docstring says "`#` splits arguments and `;` truncates them", but _split_args uses `sep = "#" if (lean and "#" in argtext) else (";" if ";" in argtext else ",")`. So Lean `H[X + Y ; μ]` becomes `h[v0+v1,?]` and never matches the paper's `h[v0+v1]`. README's own example `d[X ; μ # Y ; μ] ≤ H[X + Y ; μ]` yields `pat:le(d[v0,v1]|h[v0+v1,?])`. 210 of 545 bracket applications in pfr.jsonl heads contain `;` and no `#`.

Measured with verify-bench --patterns draws (seed 0):
- Correct proposals: pattern fire rate 15/176 (8.5%) -> 36/176 (20.5%).
- Siblings: 4/176, unchanged.
- Wrong-namespace: 0/21 -> 1/21, so README's 0.0% on that row would no longer hold.

Fix: when `lean`, use `sep = "#" if "#" in argtext else ","`. _canon_arg already drops whatever follows `;`.

Review status: verified independently (the re-run reproduced 15/176 -> 36/176).
acceptance_criteria:
- A unittest checks that the Lean and LaTeX forms of `d[X;Y] ≤ H[X+Y]` emit the same `pat:` feature.
- Handoff reports verify-bench --patterns before/after.
- The stale verify.py comment citing 8.6%/0.6% fire rates is corrected.
- README numbers are left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: leanscan truncates declaration heads at 3 lines, starving the structural reranker
description:
Problem: scan_file's head loop stops after 3 lines (`while k < n and len(head_lines) < 3 ...`). It also stops on the substring test `"where" in head_lines[-1]`, so a line containing `nowhere` stops it. The result is then cut at 400 characters. 15,173 idx_full heads end before the signature does, including 109 of the 212 PFR gold answers. For example, `theorem long_sig (a b c : Nat) (h1 : a ≤ b) (h2 : b ≤ c) :` loses its conclusion. StructReranker builds its skeletons from `head`.

Measured with the `mathgraph bench` config, heads only:
- +structural r@1: 34 -> 42 of 176 (lost 2 / gained 10, exact McNemar p = 0.039).
- +structural r@5: 67 -> 77 (6/16, p = 0.052, not significant).
- The 439 blueprint pairs are unchanged (0/0).
- The verify pattern path accepts 15 -> 22 of 176 correct proposals.

Fix: extend the head until a line contains `:=` or a word-bounded `where` (re.search(r"\bwhere\b", ...)), or until the next declaration, attribute or docstring starts. Raise the 400-character cap to about 3,000.

Review status: verified independently (re-run under the same config; same counts and p-values).
acceptance_criteria:
- A unittest covers the long_sig and `nowhere` probes.
- Handoff reports paired lost/gained with p-values, and does not call the r@5 gain significant.
- README numbers are left to mathgraph-dem.12.

title: Index generated declarations from the elaborated ground truth (simps, fields, ext, to_dual, real to_additive twins)
description:
Problem: this is the second root cause of false `nonexistent` verdicts (the first is mathgraph-dem.2).
- When mathlib_elab.jsonl is present, index.build only DROPS to_additive guesses that are missing from it (`if new not in truth: ...dropped; continue`). It never adds the real twin.
- names.to_additive_name returns None, or a wrong name, for whole shapes:
  - `Finset.Ici_one_eq_univ` -> None
  - `Filter.instOne` -> None
  - `Function.mulSupport_one` -> `Function.mulSupport_zero`, while the real twin is `Function.support_zero`
- `to_dual` is ignored entirely: 3,917 attribute lines in Mathlib, 0 references in mathgraph/.

99,334 Mathlib ground-truth names are missing from idx_mathlib. Heuristic attribution:

| cause | names |
|---|---|
| compiler auxiliaries | ~26.4k |
| auto-named instances | ~16.9k |
| @[simps] | ~15.0k |
| structure/class fields | ~11.7k |
| scanner (mathgraph-dem.2) | ~9.3k |
| to_additive | >= 4.1k |
| @[ext] | ~3.7k |
| @[reassoc] | ~3.4k |
| where-auxiliaries | ~3.2k |
| to_dual | >= 2.2k |

Example: all 18 Finset.addEnergy* names are absent, so verify calls Finset.addEnergy `nonexistent` -- in a tool benchmarked on additive combinatorics.

Note: `--corpus idx_elaborated` already contains these names. But it also brings compiler boilerplate, its thresholds were never fitted, and the artifact is stale (mathgraph-dem.9).

Fix: when ground truth is present, append the mathlib_elab.jsonl rows from covered Mathlib modules whose names the scan lacks. They already have index shape (name, kind, module, type). Mark them with provenance `elaborated`. Skip compiler auxiliaries using the boilerplate filter README's idx_elaborated section already names (rec, noConfusion, mk.inj, sizeOf_spec, inst*/eq_N/match_N). On covered modules the to_additive guesser becomes redundant.

Review status: partially verified: counts and examples reproduced. The verifier notes idx_elaborated already contains these names (see below).
acceptance_criteria:
- Finset.addEnergy, Finset.Ici_zero_eq_univ, Function.support_zero and Set.ext_iff resolve in the rebuilt idx_mathlib.
- A unittest covers a small ground-truth fixture.
- meta.json reports how many rows were added, by provenance.
- Handoff reports the paired effect. Thresholds are refit in mathgraph-dem.11.

title: Cleanup, metadata, CLI and agent-instruction fixes
description:
From the 2026-10-16/17 multi-agent review of mathgraph (8 review dimensions plus a completeness pass; critical/high findings went to an independent adversarial verifier). The review was read-only; numbers below were measured on the local corpus (mathlib4 b44f89d, pfr 68730da). 'Review status' on each bead says how well its claim was checked -- re-check single-reviewer claims before acting on them.

Dead weight, licensing metadata, CLI behaviour and stale agent instructions. Independent of the index rebuild.

title: Score Lean Finder (8.2B) on the gold negative arm; needs a >=24 GB GPU
description: mathgraph-br3 scored general-purpose encoders (bge-small/base: 57% precision at 10% coverage; the 90% target is excluded). The question about the published mathlib-specific systems is still open. Lean Finder (delta-lab-ai/lean-finder, Qwen3 8.2B, ships a mathlib index) doesn't fit on a 16 GB Mac, and Claude Code cloud sessions have no GPU. Needs a >=24 GB GPU box. The absent arm requires embedding the ~250k-declaration idx_full/idx_mathlib corpus ourselves: Lean Finder's shipped index is mathlib-only, with no PFR rows, so it can't score the present arm. Run bench_pretrained.py with the same pre-registered protocol (the model may need its own query/doc formatting from its card).
acceptance_criteria: Same table as the README br3 section, with Wilson CIs, for Lean Finder; any absent-arm answers at 10% audited against mathlib source.
notes: 2026-10 review (single reviewer, not independently verified): Lean Finder's GitHub README (fetched 2026-10-16) says 'A single GPU with at least 16GB of VRAM is required', and each supported mathlib version (v4.19.0, v4.24.0, v4.28.0) ships a FAISS index of precomputed corpus embeddings. A mathlib-only index is what the absent arm and the new paper->mathlib arm need, so the run needs ~1.4k query encodes (350 PFR + arm M + 1,016 PFR rows for the present arm), not a 250k-row corpus embed on >=24 GB. Caveat: the shipped index is a different mathlib version from our pin (b44f89d), so relabel the absent arm against that corpus's names. Strip PFR docstrings first (mathgraph-dem.1). Still not runnable on the 16 GB Mac or in the sandbox (no GPU): needs one rented 16 GB GPU.

title: QUICKSTART.md:27-28 setup-output numbers (~231k declarations, ~1,071 pairs) are stale

title: README.md:1202-1209 'shipped benchmark' section describes freeze_bench.py's data card as stale-prone in a way the code no longer is
description:
README.md's 'The shipped benchmark' section, lines 1202-1209, says: 'freeze_bench.py's data card is a static template whose text does not recompute from the corpus it's actually run on -- its stated counts and baseline numbers can go stale independently of tasks.jsonl.'

This was true before commit 591d4a9 but that same commit already fixed the 'counts' half of this claim: mathgraph/freeze_bench.py's CARD template (around line 90) now reads '$N_PRES + $N_ABS statements ... These counts are computed from the corpus that generated this release's tasks.jsonl, not hardcoded', and main() calls string.Template(CARD).substitute(N_PRES=n_pres, N_ABS=n_abs) (freeze_bench.py line ~179) with real counts derived from the corpus at run time. So the counts no longer 'go stale independently of tasks.jsonl' -- they're templated from it directly.

The 'baseline numbers' half of the README claim is still accurate for a different reason than stated: the CARD's Baselines table has 'lexical + calibrated abstention | see note | see note | see note' (freeze_bench.py lines ~122-136) -- it's not computed at all (by design, with a footnote explaining why and how to reproduce it yourself), not 'stale from not recomputing'.

Confirmed by reading mathgraph/freeze_bench.py directly (git show 591d4a9 -- mathgraph/freeze_bench.py) and comparing against the README prose at README.md:1191-1210, both read in full this session.

What would close this: reword README.md:1202-1209 so it accurately reflects the current freeze_bench.py -- the row counts ARE templated from the run corpus (verified, not a staleness risk), the baseline numbers table is deliberately left as 'see note' rather than computed (a different kind of caveat than 'goes stale'). Keep the underlying caution (don't trust anything printed inside a generated bench_release/README.md's baseline table without independently reproducing it) but stop claiming the counts can drift when the code was just changed in this same commit to prevent that.
close_reason: Reworded README.md:1209-1220 to match freeze_bench.py as of commit 591d4a9: counts are templated from the run corpus (verified via string.Template(CARD).substitute(N_PRES=n_pres, N_ABS=n_abs) at freeze_bench.py:179, same n_pres/n_abs used for tasks.jsonl), so they can no longer drift apart from tasks.jsonl within one release -- only across releases/corpora. Baseline table's abstention row is deliberately left as 'see note', not stale. Underlying caution to not trust a bench_release/README.md number without reproducing it is kept.

the present-arm count has independently drifted from 175->176 everywhere else it's measured in
this repo (see mathgraph-3gu, mathgraph-etj, mathgraph-1f3), it's very likely that if
bench_release/ was frozen once at/near that initial commit, README:1105's "175+174" is an
accurate description of THAT frozen snapshot -- but the README doesn't say when it was frozen or
against what commit, so a reader can't tell it's historical rather than a live claim, and can't
tell whether it's still the version anyone would get by regenerating.

This is coupled to mathgraph-q3z (the freeze_bench.py CARD hardcodes the same stale 175/174) --
read that bead first, since fixing the generator changes what "regenerate and check" would even
produce.

Fix (pick one):
(a) If a real bench_release/ artifact is published/distributed elsewhere (ask a human -- I
    could not find one in this repo), get its actual tasks.jsonl and count present/absent rows
    directly, then either confirm 175/174 is correct-as-frozen-history and add a provenance note
    (commit hash or date it was frozen at), or correct the counts if it turns out to have been
    regenerated since.
(b) If no such artifact exists yet, reword README:1105 to describe what running
    `python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench` (after mathgraph-q3z is fixed) produces NOW, rather than
    asserting fixed counts.

Evidence that closes this: either the located real bench_release/tasks.jsonl's actual row counts
matching the README text (with provenance noted), or updated README text plus a note on how (a)
was ruled out.
notes: Resolved via option (b): no real bench_release/ artifact found anywhere (find + git log --all both empty, re-confirmed). freeze_bench.py confirmed untouched (mathgraph-q3z still open/unfixed, out of scope here). Reworded README.md 'The shipped benchmark' section to (1) state bench_release/ is generated on demand via 'python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench', not a checked-in frozen artifact, (2) drop the unverifiable '175 present + 174 absent' claim rather than substitute a guessed number, (3) add caveat that freeze_bench.py's CARD template doesn't recompute its counts from the corpus it's run against, so even a freshly generated bench_release/README.md's numbers can't be trusted until q3z lands -- point reader at tasks.jsonl instead. Full suite: 76/76 pass (MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests), better than documented one-failure baseline because a prior uncommitted session already fixed the 175->176 test expectation. Handoff: sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-036.md
