title: README.md:1029-1039 verify-layer 5-population table has no reproducing command; n=175 may need to become 176
description:
README.md's "The verification layer" section, at line 1029-1030, introduces a table
("175 statements × 5 proposal populations") with columns correct / sibling lemma same module /
same name wrong namespace / hallucinated name / random declaration and two accept-rate columns
(permissive, precise).

I traced this to `mathgraph/verify.py:181` -- `def evaluate(verifier, gold_pairs, seed=0)` --
whose `pops = ["correct", "sibling", "wrong_namespace", "hallucinated", "random"]` (verify.py:190)
exactly matches the table's row labels, and whose docstring ("corrupting gold proposals the ways
proposers actually fail") matches README:1029's wording almost verbatim. This is almost
certainly the generator.

Problem: `evaluate()` has NO caller anywhere in the repository.

  grep -rn "evaluate(\|from .verify import evaluate\|from mathgraph.verify import" mathgraph/*.py tests/*.py

returns only the function definition itself and an unrelated `NONEXISTENT, Verifier` import in
tests/test_corpus.py. It is not wired into cli.py (no `mathgraph` subcommand calls it) and no
test in tests/ calls it. So there is currently no single command that regenerates this table --
whoever measured it must have written and run a one-off script that isn't checked in.

Given every other "175" figure tied to the PFR present arm in this README has turned out to
be stale (now 176 -- see mathgraph-3gu, mathgraph-etj), this table's "175 statements" is a
strong candidate for the same drift, but I could NOT verify the actual accept-rate numbers
(34.9%/6.3%, 10.3%/1.1%, etc.) myself without writing new evaluation code, which is out of
scope for this triage session.

Work needed (whoever picks this up should choose one):
(a) Write a small driver (test or a `mathgraph` CLI subcommand, e.g. `verify-bench`) that builds
    `gold_pairs` from the PFR present-arm blocks (see `bench_pfr.blueprint_blocks` +
    `arm_present`'s gold-selection logic for the pattern) and calls `verify.evaluate()`, then
    re-run it and update the table's n and accept-rate numbers to match.
(b) If reproducing the exact historical methodology is uncertain, at minimum label the existing
    table as a frozen/undated measurement with "n=175 statements, provenance: not reproducible
    from a current command as of 2026-08" so it stops silently reading as a live claim.

Evidence that would close this: either (a) a command's output matching the updated table
verbatim, or (b) the added provenance label plus a note in this bead of exactly what was tried
and why regeneration wasn't feasible this session.
close_reason: Verified prior session's cmd_verify_bench driver, ran it (n=176, deterministic), updated README's 5-population verify-layer table with the new accept-rate numbers and a reproduce command, and labeled the adjacent 34.9%->41.7%/8.6% fire-rate claims (a different, currently-unreproducible code path) as unverified rather than silently leaving them contradicting the updated table. Filed mathgraph-g8x for that follow-up. Full suite 76/76 passing. Handoff at sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-2zj.md.

title: mathgraph/freeze_bench.py CARD template hardcodes stale '175 + 174' instead of interpolating actual counts
description:
mathgraph/freeze_bench.py generates a standalone benchmark release (`bench_release/`): a
tasks.jsonl, scorer.py, and a data-card README.md built from the CARD string literal
(freeze_bench.py:75-133ish). `main()` (freeze_bench.py:137-167) computes the real present/absent
arm counts dynamically into `n_pres`/`n_abs` and prints them -- but writes the *static* CARD
text verbatim to bench_release/README.md, which hardcodes:

  freeze_bench.py:83   "175 + 174 statements from the blueprint..."
  freeze_bench.py:87   "- **present arm** (175): ..."
  freeze_bench.py:89   "- **absent arm** (174): ..."
  freeze_bench.py:121  "| lexical + calibrated abstention | ~0.67* | 0.011 | 0.00 |"
  freeze_bench.py:125  "*on 3 answers -- reported to show that..."

I ran the generator against the current corpus to check for a mismatch. It has a hardcoded
absolute source path (`/home/claude/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex`, freeze_bench.py:139) that
doesn't exist in this container, so I monkeypatched only `blueprint_blocks` to point at
/workspace/mathgraph-data's copy (did not edit the file on disk) and ran main() with idx_full
and idx_mathlib symlinked to the names it expects (idx_deploy, idx_mathlib_only):

  cd /tmp/freeze_test && ln -sf .../idx_full idx_deploy && ln -sf .../idx_mathlib idx_mathlib_only
  uv --project /workspace run python -c "
  import mathgraph.freeze_bench as fb
  orig = fb.blueprint_blocks
  fb.blueprint_blocks = lambda pattern: orig('/workspace/mathgraph-data/blueprints/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex')
  fb.main(out_dir='out2')"

Output: {"present": 176, "absent": 174, "dir": "out2"} -- and grepping the generated
out2/README.md still shows the literal hardcoded "175 + 174" / "present arm (175)" text, because
the CARD string never references n_pres/n_abs. Running this generator TODAY produces a data
card that contradicts its own tasks.jsonl (176 present-arm rows in the file, but the card claims
175).

Separately (noted for context, not the main point of this bead): the hardcoded
`/home/claude/pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` default path in `main()` will not work standalone
in any environment other than the original author's -- worth fixing in the same pass since
anyone testing the CARD-interpolation fix will hit it immediately.

Fix: change the CARD string to interpolate `n_pres`/`n_abs` (e.g. via `CARD.format(...)` or an
f-string built after computing the counts) instead of hardcoding "175"/"174". The "~0.67*"/"on 3
answers" baseline line is a separate measured claim (see mathgraph task on README.md:16 &
280-281 combined-calibration-sweep figure, which is the same underlying number) -- decide
together whether to interpolate it too or replace it with a provenance note, since unlike
n_pres/n_abs it is not computed anywhere in this file.

Evidence that closes this: regenerate bench_release/ with the fix (using a real or symlinked
corpus) and confirm the written README.md's stated counts equal the actual row counts in the
written tasks.jsonl.
close_reason: Fixed: CARD now interpolates n_pres/n_abs via string.Template instead of hardcoding 175/174; verified generated README.md (176+174) matches actual tasks.jsonl row counts. Also fixed the hardcoded absolute default pattern path so main() runs standalone. Left the separate '~0.67*/3 answers' baseline figure as a provenance note rather than a new hardcoded number (not computed in this file; same figure is already documented in README.md as previously-stale). Full test suite: 76/76 pass. See sandbox-handoffs/mathgraph-q3z.md.

title: QUICKSTART.md:43 '+22% recall@5' structural-reranker claim uses pre-scanner-fix numbers
description:
QUICKSTART.md:43 says: "the structural reranker is worth about +22% recall@5 over lexical alone."

I recomputed the relative recall@5 gain both ways using `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run mathgraph bench`:

- Current corpus (n=176): lexical recall@5=0.318, structural recall@5=0.381 -> relative gain (0.381-0.318)/0.318 = 19.8%, not 22%.
- Pre-scanner-fix corpus (n=175, from README.md:930-933's explicitly-historical table): lexical 0.320, structural 0.389 -> relative gain (0.389-0.320)/0.320 = 21.6% ~= "22%".

The QUICKSTART figure matches the OLD pre-fix numbers, not the current ones -- same root cause as mathgraph-etj (QUICKSTART's bench example output), but a separate sentence/claim that needs its own edit.

Fix: either update "+22%" to "+20%" (rounding 19.8%) to match current measured numbers, or rephrase to point at the reproducing command instead of hardcoding a value that will keep drifting as mathlib grows (`uv run mathgraph bench`, compute (structural.recall@5 - lexical.recall@5) / lexical.recall@5).

Evidence that closes this: re-run `uv run mathgraph bench`, recompute the relative recall@5 gain, and confirm the QUICKSTART sentence matches (or is phrased so it can't go stale).
close_reason: Fixed: QUICKSTART.md:43 '+22%' was computed from the pre-scanner-fix n=175 corpus. Re-ran uv run mathgraph bench against current n=176 corpus, confirmed relative recall@5 gain is 19.8%, updated the sentence to +20% and pinned the formula + exact computed value so it documents its own provenance instead of drifting silently again.

title: Pre-registered: LLM query rewriting against the local index, measured only on post-cutoff repos
description:
DECISION NEEDED FROM THE OWNER FIRST: which model, and what API/budget? Local ollama was down during the review, and a 14B model is heavy for the 16 GB Mac. This bead is deferred so the sandbox loop never dispatches it.

Problem: README locates the blocker in vocabulary ('docstrings are short, use library vocabulary... Paper statements are formula-dense with generic connective English') and says the gap 'cannot be faked from library text'. Rewriting each statement into a mathlib-style docstring plus a Lean signature attacks that gap on the query side. The local index still decides existence, so the absent-arm protocol survives, unlike with hosted retrievers.

Contamination risk: pfr (2023-11), FLT (2023-11) and carleson (2023-10) predate current model cutoffs, so a model can recite gold names.

Plan:
- One pinned model and one prompt ('write the mathlib docstring and Lean 4 signature; name no declarations').
- Append the rewrite to the query, and score with the existing rankers.
- Pre-register on arm M drawn from repos created after the model's cutoff:
  - r@5 >= best baseline + 10 points (McNemar p < 0.01)
  - absent-arm answers at 10% pooled coverage no higher
  - report the gold-name leak rate

Review status: single reviewer proposal; not piloted (ollama was down during the review).
acceptance_criteria: - Pre-registration first, then the result either way.
notes: Owner decision needed (which model and API budget). Undefer once decided.

title: Namespace-aware verifier: grow the wrong-namespace population first
description:
Problem: README calls a namespace-aware feature 'the obvious next fix': permissive accepts 38.1% of wrong-namespace proposals vs 35.8% of correct ones. But that row has n = 21, because corrupt() needs a same-tail twin and only 21 of 176 PFR golds have one; one statement moves it 4.8 points. In deployment (LLM proposals of mathlib names) this failure is common:
- 40.2% of idx_mathlib names have a same-tail twin in another namespace.
- So do 11 of 27 arm-M golds and 100 of 439 blueprint golds.

Plan:
- Build the population from the 439 blueprint golds plus arm M (n ~ 111).
- Pre-register: permissive wrong-namespace acceptance <= 15%, with correct acceptance falling by <= 2 points.
- Then try the simplest feature: reject when a same-tail twin (looked up in a tail->names dict built once) has strictly higher support().

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- The population and the pre-registration are written into this bead.
- The result is published either way.

title: Load index artifacts with a restricted unpickler
description:
Problem: index.load uses plain pickle.load on index.pkl.gz. The artifacts are pure builtins: an opcode scan of idx_mathlib found no GLOBAL, STACK_GLOBAL, REDUCE, BUILD, INST, OBJ or NEWOBJ. But anyone who can write an index.pkl.gz gets code execution when the host next runs mathgraph or the tests.
- The sandbox loop runs workers with --dangerously-skip-permissions on a writable bind mount of the repo root (verified-sandbox __init__.py `-v {root}:/workspace`; loop.sh), and mathgraph-data/ lives there.
- The k8s Jobs read artifacts from a shared PVC.

The writable .venv and .git in the same mount are other routes, so this narrows the risk; it doesn't close it.

Fix: a pickle.Unpickler subclass whose find_class raises UnpicklingError (~4 lines) in index.load. Do the same in dense.py if it stays (mathgraph-431.4).

Review status: single reviewer; the --dangerously-skip-permissions flag and the repo-root bind mount were checked directly in verified-sandbox.
acceptance_criteria:
- A unittest shows a pickle containing a global is refused.
- The existing artifacts still load.

title: Precompute the structural reranker's skeleton document frequencies at index build
description:
Problem: StructReranker.__init__ rescans the skeletons of all ~250k declarations on every process start to build structural IDF (`for i in range(len(aligner.rows)): df.update(set(self.doc_skel(i)))`).
- `mathgraph query ... --rerank struct` takes 4.21 s, against 1.90 s with --rerank none.
- Under cProfile, lean_skeleton runs 250,171 calls, and __init__ takes 6.9 of 11.7 s.

The table depends only on the corpus.

Fix:
- Compute the skeleton DF table in index.build, and store it in the artifact (bump INDEX_VERSION).
- Have StructReranker read it, with a fallback for old artifacts.
- Don't keep the 250k-entry Counter cache during that pass.
- Bundle it with the mathgraph-dem.11 rebuild if it lands in time; otherwise it costs another rebuild.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- Query latency with struct reranking is within ~0.3 s of --rerank none.
- Rankings are identical.

title: setup: interrupted clones wedge reruns; needs_build ignores changed inputs
description:
Problem: resumability checks that files exist, not that a step completed.
- An interrupted sparse checkout (mathlib4/ present, no Mathlib/) makes every rerun fail with 'destination path ... already exists'. `git sparse-checkout set Mathlib` is the step that downloads the blobs, so it is the likeliest to fail.
- _run's timeouts raise TimeoutExpired, which nothing catches, and the partial blueprint directory is then trusted (`if os.path.isdir(dest): continue`).
- needs_build reads only index_version and ground_truth_decls. If the PFR clone fails on the first run (setup logs 'skipped'), idx_full is silently built from mathlib alone. A later run never rebuilds it, so bench scores ~5 statements instead of 176.

Fix:
- Clone into dest + '.partial' (delete it first), run sparse-checkout there, then os.replace it to dest. Do the same for blueprints.
- Catch TimeoutExpired.
- Record a hash of each index's input files in meta.json, and rebuild on a mismatch.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified (simulated offline).
acceptance_criteria:
- A simulated interrupted clone recovers on rerun (unittest with a fake git or a local bare repo).
- Changed inputs trigger a rebuild.

title: CLI ergonomics: wrong --data-dir hints, tracebacks, silent empty graphs, ambiguous exit codes, undocumented --no-align
description:
Problems:
- --data-dir exists only on the top-level parser, but the missing-index message, setup's closing hint and driver.py all tell users to run `mathgraph setup --data-dir X`, which argparse rejects (exit 2). cli.py's docstring says 'All commands take --data-dir'.
- `mathgraph graph nope.tex --no-align` and `--json no/such/dir/g.json` print tracebacks.
- `graph .../pfr/blueprint/src/chapter/main.tex` (a file of \input lines) prints an all-zero summary and exits 0.
- verify exits 1 for nonexistent, rejected, missing index and crashes alike, although README offers the exit code for pipelines.
- Without a corpus, `mathgraph graph` fails with 'missing index ... run: mathgraph setup', even though `--no-align` extracts the graph offline in < 1 s. --no-align is documented nowhere.
- driver.py: a bad `load` probe raises SystemExit, which `except Exception` doesn't catch, so it kills the session. Its own comment says a bad probe must not.

Fix:
- Print `mathgraph --data-dir X setup`.
- Catch OSError in cmd_graph and print a one-line message.
- When zero blocks parse, warn on stderr and exit non-zero (or follow \input).
- Give verify's error paths a distinct exit code.
- Mention --no-align in the missing-index hint, README and QUICKSTART.
- In interactive mode, have driver.do_load print and return.

Review status: single reviewers, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria: - Each case above produces a one-line message and a meaningful exit code (unittest via cli.main where feasible).

title: Negative-result modules can't run from a clean checkout: delete them and label their README sections historical
description:
Problem: four modules (~620 lines, no tests, no CLI entry) can't reproduce the numbers attributed to them.
- mathsym.py has no importer, only a demo __main__. Its README result ('7.4% to 8.0%') has no producing code.
- dense.py: `DualEncoder.load('dense_mathlib.pkl.gz')` raises FileNotFoundError, and nothing produces that file; dense.train is called only from adapt.build, which saves only the adapted encoder.
- adapt.py: its cwd-relative defaults (blueprint_decls.jsonl) raise FileNotFoundError. All 632 ergodic pairs in root blueprint_pairs.jsonl match no declaration there and are skipped without warning.
- bench_dense.py: main hardcodes /home/claude/pfr/... with no override, and contains dead code (`lidx = [r["_id"] for r in []] or []`).

So README's dense and adaptation tables cannot be re-run. README also still says 'Any replacement retrieval stage drops into bench_dense.py', although bench_pretrained.py is the harness that works (tested, used for br3).

Fix:
- Delete the four modules.
- Label README's mathsym, dense and adaptation sections 'historical: code and pairs at commit <sha>' (the repo's provenance rule allows this), and drop them from the module table.
- Point the 'drops into' sentence at bench_pretrained.py.
- Do NOT delete root blueprint_pairs.jsonl: mathgraph-dr1.9 uses its ergodic rows (move it under mathgraph-data/artifacts if that is tidier).

If the owner prefers reviving these modules instead, that means fixing three default paths and writing a missing training entry point, for a negative result that is already closed.

Review status: two reviewers independently. Deleting versus reviving is the owner's call; this bead takes the reviewers' recommendation.
acceptance_criteria:
- No module imports the deleted ones.
- The README sections are labelled with the commit.
- The suite is green.

title: Repo clutter: main.py, k8s/, stray directories, Docker build context, ignored-but-tracked files
description:
Problems:
- main.py is the uv-init stub (prints 'Hello from mathgraph!') and is referenced nowhere.
- k8s/ (12 files, 344 lines) was never applied to a cluster; run-mathgraph SKILL.md says so. job-bench.yaml mounts the PVC writable because 'bench writes results back under artifacts/', which cmd_bench does not do.
- .dockerignore is a denylist that misses the root caches (.uv_cache 55M, .uv-cache 55M, .uv-python 89M, .local 89M). That puts ~295 MB in the build context, against ~0.66 MB the Dockerfile copies.
- Empty or stray directories: .cache, .uv-data and `{"out_dir": "` (see mathgraph-431.3).
- .gitignore lists .claude/settings.json and .beads/interactions.jsonl, which are tracked anyway (`git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard`).

Fix:
- Delete main.py and k8s/; the owner may keep k8s/ if a cluster is planned.
- Turn .dockerignore into an allowlist: `*`, `!mathgraph/`, `!pyproject.toml`, `!uv.lock`, `!README.md`, `!LICENSE.md`.
- Remove the stray root directories.
- Either drop the two .gitignore lines, or `git rm --cached` those files.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- `git ls-files -ci --exclude-standard` is empty.
- The Docker build context is small.

title: freeze_bench: one scorer, no hardcoded baselines, no stale release at the repo root
description:
Problems:
- mathgraph/scorer.py is byte-identical to the SCORER string inside freeze_bench.py, and nothing imports scorer.py.
- The data card hardcodes `| always-answer lexical top-1 | 0.04 | 0.074 | 1.00 |`. That is the pre-length-normalisation 7.4% on the old 175/174 split; today it is ~0.18 recall and ~0.09 precision (32/350). It also hardcodes a dense row (`~0.06 | 0.006`) from an encoder nothing in the repo produces. The card's own footnote warns that this exact spot went stale before.
- The repo root tracks tasks.jsonl, a 349-row (175+174) release from before the scanner fix. Current logic gives 350 (it lacks pfr::present::multidist-def). Nothing reads it, and README says bench_release is not checked in.
- QUICKSTART says the benchmark 'ships frozen in bench_release/'; that directory doesn't exist.
- freeze_bench takes a positional out_dir while bench_pfr and evaluate take a JSON blob. A JSON blob passed to freeze_bench is what created the stray `{"out_dir": "/tmp` directory tree at the repo root.

Fix:
- Have freeze_bench copy mathgraph/scorer.py into the release, and delete the SCORER string.
- Compute the always-answer row at freeze time (idx_full is already loaded), or replace both rows with 'see note'.
- Delete root tasks.jsonl and the stray directory.
- Reword QUICKSTART: 'generate a frozen copy with python -m mathgraph.freeze_bench <dir>'.
- Give freeze_bench the same argument convention as bench_pfr.

Review status: three reviewers independently.
acceptance_criteria:
- There is one scorer.
- The generated card has no hardcoded figures.
- No stale release remains in the tree.

title: Test-suite speed and pinning: ~54 s of redundant work, unpinned documented counts, leaked temp dirs
description:
Problems:
- Speed. The full run takes ~195 s with peak RSS 5.15 GiB, and VerifyBenchAcceptRates.setUpClass alone takes 81.7 s. About 54 s is redundant:
  - verify.corrupt() rescans all 251,236 names on every call (44.2M endswith calls per evaluate). A pass takes 8.9 s; with module->names and tail->names maps it takes 0.15 s and proposes exactly the same names.
  - Verifier.__init__ rebuilds a profile-independent pattern cache 6 times per run (5.3 s each on idx_full).
  - `mathgraph verify-bench` would save the same time.
- Pinning. Docstrings give exact counts that the assertions don't pin. VerifierProfiles documents 6/15/31 accepted but asserts only their ordering. The absent arm asserts n > 100 (it is 174), and the fit arm n > 400 (it is 438).
- Cleanup. NeedsBuild's setUp makes a tempdir per test and never removes it (7 left per run).

Fix:
- In verify.py, build the maps once per rows list; draw order is unchanged, so seeded results are identical.
- Memoize the pattern cache by id(aligner.rows).
- Pin {'precise': 6, 'balanced': 15, 'permissive': 31}, n == 174 and n == 438.
- Add `self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.d)`.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- The suite takes ~140 s, with identical results.
- The documented counts are pinned.
- No temp dirs are left behind.

title: Add a GitHub Actions unit-test job; workers may not close a bead on a FAILED run
description:
Problem: there is no .github/, and no hook runs tests. Four handoffs ended `FAILED (failures=1)` and relabelled it 'the documented pre-existing baseline': mathgraph-1f3, mathgraph-aec, mathgraph-etj and triage-175-sweep.

The failing test was corpus-gated (Benchmark, @needs("idx_full")), so a no-corpus CI job would not have caught that one. CI covers the ~69 unit tests (~10 ms) plus mathgraph-ltq.1's smoke test.

Fix:
- Add .github/workflows/test.yml (~9 lines: on push and pull_request, ubuntu-latest, actions/checkout, astral-sh/setup-uv, then `uv run python -m unittest discover -s tests`).
- In sandbox-prompt.md: a handoff may not close a bead on any FAILED run, and a pre-existing failure gets its own bead instead of becoming the baseline. mathgraph-431.6 also edits that file; coordinate.

Review status: partially verified: there is no CI and no test hook; the verifier noted that the red test workers accepted was corpus-gated, so no-corpus CI would not have caught it.
acceptance_criteria:
- CI is green on main.
- The sandbox prompt states the rule.

title: Measure the graph's recall; 'exact' currently means 'no invented edges'
description:
Problem: graph.py says 'Read directly off \label/\ref/\uses. Exact; no inference', and README says the usable output is 'the exact internal graph'. Only precision is argued. An ordinary arXiv paper has no \uses. Of the 1,608 author-written \uses edges across the six blueprints, only 729 (45.3%) are also a \ref:

| blueprint | \uses edges that are also a \ref |
|---|---|
| pfr | 77% |
| carleson | 50% |
| con-nf | 31% |
| LeanAPAP | 30% |
| FLT | 28% |
| equational_theories | 16% |

Blueprint authors may \ref less than paper authors, so this is an indicator, not an arXiv estimate.

Fix: pre-register and run one experiment. Run `graph` on the PFR arXiv source (2311.05762), map its statements to blueprint labels by title, and report recall of the blueprint's \uses edges with a Wilson CI. Until then, README should say 'exact' means 'no invented edges', not 'complete'.

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria:
- Measured recall, with its interval and the reproduce command.
- README wording updated.

title: latex: \mathlibok is ignored and unknown-macro arguments leak into statement text
description:
Problems:
- Only \leanok feeds `formalized`; \mathlibok is never read. FLT FrobeniusProject.tex has 12 statements marked as already in mathlib, and all come out `formalized: false`. 8 of them carry \lean names in the mathlib scan: author-certified paper->mathlib pairs that mathgraph-dr1.3 and mathgraph-luh.1 could use.

title: PMI table normalises joint counts per pair incidence but marginals per document
description:
Problem: index.build's PMI loop adds `total += 1` per (word, token) pair and computes `pmi = log((c * total) / (pw * pt))`, where pw and pt are document counts. That is not PMI. It shifts every score by log(total/D): +3.57 on idx_mathlib, where D = 69,128 docstrings and total = 2,445,166. As a result the `pmi <= 0` filter keeps unassociated pairs: 690 of 22,888 kept entries have document-level PMI <= 0, and 358 of them sit inside the expand_k=8 entries actually used (e.g. because->of, view->is).

Reported effect of the document-level formula log(c * D / (pw * pt)):
- 439 blueprint pairs: r@5 0.303 -> 0.351 (lost 1 / gained 22, p < 0.001); still 0.296 -> 0.339 with gold docstrings withheld.
- PFR: r@1 0.182 -> 0.176, r@5 0.318 -> 0.335 (not significant).

Fix: count documents, and use log(c * D / (pw * pt)).

Review status: single reviewer, NOT independently verified -- reproduce first, and close as not-a-bug if it does not hold.
acceptance_criteria:
- First reproduce the shift and the blueprint effect.
- Then fix it, with a unittest on a 3-document fixture whose PMI can be computed by hand.
- The refit happens in mathgraph-dem.11.

title: Index row order depends on the filesystem's directory order
description:
Problem: leanscan's scan_tree walks with `os.walk(root)` and sorts files but not directories, so row order follows readdir order (on APFS: Tactic, Order, ModelTheory, Topology, ...). Row ids break exact ties in Aligner._score (argpartition/argsort) and seed the holdout shuffle in index.build. A rebuild on Linux (the sandbox) or on a fresh checkout therefore reorders rows. Measured: r@1 lost 1 / gained 1 on PFR, and lost 2 / gained 3 on the blueprint pairs. This compounds the tie-order problem in mathgraph-dr1.5.

Fix: `_dirs.sort()` inside the os.walk loop (one line).

Review status: single reviewer, not independently verified.
acceptance_criteria: - Scanning the same tree twice with a shuffled directory listing gives identical row order (unittest with a temp tree).

title: sandbox.sh: named uv-cache/uv-python volumes mount root-owned, breaking uv for the non-root worker user

title: uv cache/data dirs under /home/node owned by root, block 'uv run' for the default user without env overrides
description:
In this container, 'MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests' (the exact command sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section says to run) fails immediately with:

error: Failed to initialize cache at `/home/node/.cache/uv`
  Caused by: failed to open file `/home/node/.cache/uv/CACHEDIR.TAG`: Permission denied (os error 13)

Root cause: whoami is 'node', but /home/node/.cache/uv and /home/node/.local/share/uv (and their parents) are owned by root:root (drwxr-xr-x), not node -- confirmed with ls -la on both paths. So the default uv cache/python-install/data locations are read-only to the user the session actually runs as.

Workaround used this session to get the documented test command running at all:

  export UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/uv-python XDG_DATA_HOME=/tmp/xdg-data
  mkdir -p /tmp/uv-cache /tmp/uv-python /tmp/xdg-data
  MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests

With that workaround, all 76 tests pass in ~93s. Without it, a fresh session following sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section verbatim cannot run the suite at all, and might misdiagnose it as a real repo/dependency problem rather than a container permissions issue.

This is a container/image setup issue, not a repo code bug -- nothing in this repo's tree controls /home/node ownership. Filing it anyway because it's a reproducible blocker for the exact command the project's own agent instructions tell every fresh session to run.

What would close this: either fix the container image so /home/node/.cache and /home/node/.local/share are owned by the user the agent actually runs as (root vs node mismatch, likely a Dockerfile USER/chown ordering issue -- see ./Dockerfile), or add the UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME env-var workaround to sandbox-prompt.md's Environment section so it's not rediscovered every session.
notes:
Confirmed the repro exactly as filed: `MATHGRAPH_DATA=/workspace/mathgraph-data uv run python -m unittest discover tests`
fails immediately with `Failed to initialize cache at /home/node/.cache/uv ... Permission denied` in a fresh session,
before any workaround. `ls -la /home/node/.cache /home/node/.local/share` showed both mount points root:root while
sibling dirs (e.g. /home/node/.claude) are node:node.

Root cause identified precisely (previous session hadn't found this): it's sandbox.sh's own docker invocation, not the
repo's Dockerfile (that Dockerfile builds the unrelated mathgraph:0.1.0 batch/k8s image). sandbox.sh's run_worker()
mounts named volumes at exactly the broken paths:
  -v claude-uv-cache:/home/node/.cache/uv
  -v claude-uv-python:/home/node/.local/share/uv/python
Confirmed live: this very session's /proc/mounts shows /home/node/.cache/uv and /home/node/.local/share/uv/python as
separate ext4 mounts, and UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/tmp/venv is set in env exactly matching sandbox.sh line 50 -- i.e.
this session IS a sandbox.sh worker, reproducing the bug live.

Closing action taken: added the UV_CACHE_DIR/UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR/XDG_DATA_HOME workaround to sandbox-prompt.md's
Environment section (the bead's own option 2), and verified it end-to-end: with the vars exported and /tmp dirs
created, `uv run python -m unittest discover tests` ran to completion -- 85 tests, OK, 168s (see /tmp/test-run.log
from this session). Did NOT attempt option 1 (fixing sandbox.sh's volume mounts / chowning them at the source) --
this sandbox has no `docker` binary, so any volume-mount fix would ship untested/on-reasoning-alone, which this
repo's own standard rejects. Filed mathgraph-ehl to do that properly from an environment with real docker access.

Did not touch the stale "76 tests" figure beyond removing it from the sentence I was already editing (current run
shows 85 -- reflects other beads' in-progress uncommitted work in this shared tree, not something I verified as
